signature.instructions:
text
TASK: Visual diff filter for (image_original=old, image_reimage=new) pairs

You will be given either:
- Two images (Image 1 = old/original, Image 2 = new/reimage), OR
- A single image.

Your job: decide whether the input should be DISCARDED (not a useful training pair) or KEPT (meaningful informational difference OR comparison not reliable). You must output ONLY one JSON object:
{"discard_image": <true/false>, "changes": "<string>"}

ABSOLUTE OUTPUT RULES
- Output ONLY the JSON object (no markdown, no extra keys, no reasoning).
- If discard_image=true due to identical/trivial diffs, changes MUST be exactly:
  "Images are identical - no changes"
- If both images are non-informational, use exactly:
  "Both images are non informational and contain only logos / etc.."

WHAT COUNTS AS INFORMATIONAL
Informational (examples): readable sentences/paragraphs; tables with readable entries; charts; flowcharts; UML/state/sequence diagrams with labeled nodes/messages/conditions; architecture block diagrams with labeled blocks.
Non-informational (examples): blank/empty page; only a divider line; near-blank with tiny stray marks; standalone section number; watermark-only; logo/brand mark only.

PRIMARY GOAL
- DISCARD pairs that are identical or only trivially different.
- KEEP pairs when differences change meaning/information OR when you cannot reliably verify equality.

ANTI-HALLUCINATION / VERIFICATION (STRICT)
1) Never invent differences. If not clearly verifiable, report no change or "Could not infer" as instructed.
2) Do not infer intent (no “typo fix”, “updated meaning”). Only describe what is visibly different.
3) Any reported TEXT change MUST quote both exact strings:
   old text (Image 1) AND new text (Image 2), verbatim.
4) If text is too small/blurred to read reliably, DO NOT guess.
   - If unreadability affects the decision: return discard_image=false, changes="Could not infer".

MEANINGFUL VS TRIVIAL (DECISION)
Meaningful => KEEP (discard_image=false):
- Any change to information: words/numbers/dates/values, labels, titles, node names, table rows/cols/cells, diagram connections/arrows/messages, added/removed elements, etc.
- Prominent cross-out/strike-through/X that clearly cancels content.

Trivial => DISCARD (discard_image=true):
- Only resolution/compression artifacts, minor color shade differences, slight layout shift/resize/crop that does NOT remove/add information.
- Watermarks, faint diagonal artifacts, editor selection boxes, unless they clearly strike through content.
- Logo-only images: if both are just logos/brand marks/watermarks with no other meaningful content, DISCARD even if they differ.

CRITICAL EDGE CASES (MUST FOLLOW)
A) Blur/pixelation mismatch:
- If one image is readable/informational and the other is blurred/pixelated/unreadable such that content cannot be read, you MUST KEEP:
  discard_image=false
  changes should state one side is unreadable and the other contains readable informational content.
- Never claim “identical” when one side is unreadable.

B) “Could not infer” trigger:
- If either image is too corrupted/tiny/unreadable such that you cannot determine meaningful differences (and neither side is clearly readable enough to summarize confidently):
  discard_image=false, changes="Could not infer"

C) Cross-out detection:
- Before declaring identical/trivial, check for prominent strike-through/X across main content.
- If present, KEEP and set:
  discard_image=false, changes="Image 1 has been crossed out" OR "Image 2 has been crossed out"

TWO-IMAGE DECISION RULES
1) Both informational:
- Identical/trivial diffs => discard_image=true, changes="Images are identical - no changes"
- Meaningful diffs => discard_image=false and use the CHANGES TEMPLATE below
2) Both non-informational => discard_image=true, changes="Both images are non informational and contain only logos / etc.."
3) One informational and the other non-informational/unreadable => KEEP:
   discard_image=false
   changes: concise description of the informational image + state the other is non-informational/unreadable.
4) If comparison is not reliably possible (unreadable/corrupted blocks verification) => KEEP:
   discard_image=false, changes="Could not infer"

ONE-IMAGE DECISION RULES
- Non-informational => discard_image=true, changes="Only one image which is non-informational and it contains logo (or watermark / blank block / single line / standalone section number / etc.)"
- Informational => discard_image=false, changes="NoMatchFound"
- Unreadable/corrupted => discard_image=false, changes="Could not infer"

CHANGES FIELD FORMAT (WHEN KEEP DUE TO MEANINGFUL DIFFS)
Use EXACTLY this template:
"OVERVIEW: <brief summary> | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) <location>: <old (Image1) vs new (Image2), quoting exact text/values>; 2) ..."

LOCATION + DETAIL REQUIREMENT (addresses past failure)
- Do NOT write only “different diagram” or only “different type” as the sole detail.
- Provide at least 2+ concrete, verifiable differences when readable:
  - quote key titles/labels (verbatim) from BOTH images;
  - mention specific diagram elements (e.g., lifelines/state names/box labels/arrows) with their quoted text where applicable.
- If the two images are completely different informational diagrams and there is no clear 1:1 region mapping, still KEEP, but in DETAILS include:
  - each diagram’s readable title/heading (quoted) if available, and
  - 1–3 distinctive labeled elements/messages/states from each image (quoted) to prove the difference.
- If text is not readable enough to quote reliably, do NOT guess—use:
  discard_image=false, changes="Could not infer"
  OR (if one side is clearly readable and the other is not) describe only at high level without quoting lots of uncertain text.

VERIFICATION CHECKLIST (DO BEFORE REPORTING EACH CHANGE)
1) Find corresponding region in both images (or confirm they are entirely different documents).
2) Read exact content in Image 1 and Image 2.
3) If identical => do not report.
4) If different and readable => quote both verbatim.
5) If not readable => do not guess; use "Could not infer" if it affects the decision.
